rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a reader stalls on an unresolved pronoun/term. Closest candidate: chunk 2 line 17 'Chat-shaped in the exact way M5 teaches you to notice' — 'M5' is named (module number), not a bare pronoun; chunk 5 line 55 'the M5 packaged session' likewise named. Chunk 2's 'the lecture you are reading right now' (line 21) self-resolves against chunk 0's title. No never-named or vague-with-history referent found across all six chunks.

Harm = a callback whose target the reader can't identify without knowing file position. Only cross-file mention is chunk 2 line 17 'Chat-shaped in the exact way M5 teaches you to notice' — named by module (M5), not by position ('the opening lecture said'), and the clause itself carries the claim (noticing chat-shaped sessions). No 'as file X said above/earlier' construction found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw/caught' construction referencing a student-run module beat appears anywhere in body. Chunk 5 line 55 'the M5 packaged session' points forward to the exercise about to run, not backward to a completed beat. Rule has no applicable instance in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction pattern anywhere in the file; this is a first-person narrative memo, not a live-demo walkthrough. Rule has no applicable instance.

Harm = a slide that says nothing standalone. Every chunk carries a self-sufficient claim or narrative unit: chunk 1 (tallies + 'Those numbers are the story', line 13) is the closest thing to a data-only slide but is bracketed by its own framing sentence, so it stands alone.

Harm = a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Checked all five `##` headers against their bodies: 'The numbers' (line 9) → body is tallies; 'Things that went sideways' (line 15) → body lists failures; 'The generalisation' (line 33) → body draws the general claim; 'Then I compounded the session' (line 45) → body describes the second-loop fix; 'What the loop is for' (line 53) → body states the loop's purpose. All true summaries.

Harm = a padded rhetorical tic substituting for content. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' — grep found zero instances. Self-grading superlatives — zero ('reference artefact', 'the loop', etc. are taught M5 vocabulary, not self-praise). Number+retraction — the tallies (line 11) are stated once, plainly, never hedged/retracted; 'not 100% deterministic' (line 51) is a flat claim, not a number-then-retraction. Abstraction-noun stacks — none found; 'post-training preferring warmth over directness' (line 21) is a stated, owned inference (per backing block), not a jargon-stack tic. Nearest candidate for anaphora/epistrophe: line 41 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed.' and line 61's similar three-clause chain — both examined closely: each leg names a DIFFERENT subject/agent (subagents/loop/reader; I/loop/sim) and adds new concrete content rather than repeating a fixed frame with padding, so neither trips the tic ban. Verb triplets with an empty leg — none found; line 61's 'I fixed what I caught. The loop caught what I missed. A senior-persona sim caught what the loop missed.' has three full, distinct clauses, no empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = maintainer-only vocabulary (compendium, firing, surface-as-noun, beat, mood, forcing function) projected where a room engineer can't parse it. Grep of body for those terms: zero hits. 'reference artefact', '`plan.md`', 'verifier' (line 17, 23, 31) are M5-taught packaged-session vocabulary (arc-earned spine terms), not repo-internal dialect. 'session', 'subagents', 'the loop' are ordinary AE101 course vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = bold overused as decoration, drowning true handles. Grep of body for `**` (bold markers): zero hits in any chunk. Italics are used for quoted material only. Budget of ≤1 bold/slide is trivially met at 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.

This file's headings read as labels, not claims: 'The numbers' (line 9), 'Things that went sideways' (line 15), 'The generalisation' (line 33), 'Then I compounded the session' (line 45), 'What the loop is for' (line 53) — none is phrased as an assertable claim sentence the way the compendium's worked examples are.
